title: Causal effect of mandated E&S disclosure (Circular 155 / Circular 96) on the cost of capital
decisive_reason: 0/9 quasi-experiments while 6/9 papers have an unused regulatory shock in-window; P6 shows pre-2016 CSR data exist for 225 firms

title: Beyond-compliance signalling: are voluntary disclosure and substantive governance priced while compliance is not?
decisive_reason: Signalling is the declared theory (P2) but no paper separates mandated from voluntary items; P8 scores governance only above the legal minimum; P9 shows compliance labels carry no information

title: What exactly is priced: verifiable (hard) vs narrative (soft) disclosure, incremental to general transparency; heterogeneity in sensitive industries
decisive_reason: 5/5 CSR papers use binary item counts, 0/5 measure quality, 0/5 control for general disclosure although P7 shows general disclosure lowers implied COE; P3 sign outlier unexplained

title: Which channel carries the effect: liquidity/adverse selection vs investor base vs crash risk
decisive_reason: 1/9 papers tests any mechanism (P6, crash risk) and its arithmetic is inconsistent; the channels P7 theorises most explicitly are untested

title: Creditor channel: does disclosure lower the price of interest-bearing debt in a bank-dominated market?
decisive_reason: 1/9 papers studies COD (P2) with a proxy its authors concede is flawed; no Batch 2 evidence; incremental unless lender-side heterogeneity is obtainable

title: Cost-of-equity construct validity / proxy sensitivity
decisive_reason: Most pervasive weakness (5/9 CAPM; 5/8 negative COE; beta does not explain implied COE in P7) but redundant as a standalone paper: every surviving gap must report CAPM and implied COE side by side

title: Governance as credibility moderator (standalone)
decisive_reason: Standalone novelty capped by Chen et al. (2004) as cited in P9 (p.146); survives as hypothesis H2c inside F2

title: Governance compliance labels vs substance (standalone)
decisive_reason: Narrow alone; it is the governance half of the beyond-compliance theory

title: Governance reforms as quasi-experiments (standalone)
decisive_reason: India-specific novelty low (Black & Khanna 2007 cited in P8); Vietnamese governance-reform dates unverified; kept as the governance arm of F1

title: State ownership as moderator
decisive_reason: Already tested by P6 (Table 5); remaining question is direction (P6 abstract vs table); retained only as a pre-registered moderator in F1 and F3

title: Time variation / market stress
decisive_reason: No mechanism for why the effect should shift beyond generic stress; year effects become a design requirement (only 2/9 papers have them)

title: Cross-country institutional moderation
decisive_reason: Infeasible with comparable measures; prior cross-country work cited in P1 (p.62) and P9 (p.146)

title: Board structure -> COE re-run
decisive_reason: P4 and P9 add no theory; governance re-enters via F2
